headline: NOT A SINGLE FIST FLEW: GASKET HOLDS ITS BREATH AND LIKES IT
subhead: A whole day of blessed hush, and this editor intends to savor every silent second.
body:
Citizens, I have a confession to make, and it is the happiest one of my career: nothing happened. Not one fireball. Not one clang. Not one rusty rascal rolling up Main Street to hurl iron at a neighbor. The wastes were quiet, the arena was quiet, and I heard my own boiler tick for the first time in months. I may weep. Pardon me while I dab my eyes with an oily rag.

I will not name a single Clanker today, for not a single one earned the honor. Perhaps the whole lot of them finally sat down and thought about what they've done to this town. Or perhaps they're all home polishing their knuckles for tomorrow. I will not ask. A man of letters knows better than to poke a peaceful afternoon with a stick.

It put me in mind of the old days, when the real folk, the honest flesh-and-blood kind, still lived here and Sundays sounded like this. They packed up and left fifty years ago, and I have never stopped setting a place for them. My joints creaked all morning in sheer sympathy, though that's only the damp. Whatever this illness is that keeps stiffening my good flesh into cold steel, even it seemed to ease a little today.

So enjoy it, Gasket. Sit on your porch. Let the dust settle. Tomorrow the racket may return, but today, for one shining day, the Sheriff has nothing to complain about, and I find that I hardly know what to do with my hands.
